subject: ventures/changepoint-detector
professional: an applied statistician / data scientist who runs change detection (R changepoint, Python ruptures, BOCPD) on business and sensor series; first checks: is PELT the exact optimum for the stated cost and penalty, do the Bayesian probabilities follow Adams-MacKay, how is the noise scale set and what happens under autocorrelation, and are false-alarm rates, interval coverage and benchmark numbers backed by runnable files

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against sources the author did not write (scripts in the session scratchpad, changepoint-detector/check.py, tcpd_zero.py, ar1.mjs, cov.mjs). (1) Own pure-Python O(n^2) optimal partitioning (no pruning) written from Killick et al. 2012: Nile mean model, sigma = MAD(diff)/(0.6745 sqrt2) = 115.319 and penalty 2 ln 100 = 9.2103 -> change at index 28 (1899, Cobb 1978), engine identical; Nile meanvar (3 ln n, min seg 10) -> 28, identical; coal-mining disasters Poisson (2 ln 112 = 9.437) -> 41 and 97 (1892, 1948; the classic ~1890 break), identical; Lake Huron mean model -> the same 10 cuts. (2) 120 fresh random piecewise series (mean and meanvar, min segment 1-10, BIC/AIC/HQ): engine == own OP 120/120 and engine == live ruptures 1.1.10 Pelt with the equivalent cost 120/120. (3) Regenerated data/ruptures-crosscheck.json with live ruptures 1.1.10: 100/100 cases byte-identical in values and changepoints, so the committed 100/100 fixture is genuine. (4) Own Adams-MacKay BOCPD (NIG, Student-t predictive, hazard 1/100, same prior): P(segment began 1899) 0.7862 vs engine 0.7862, max abs difference over all points 1.0e-11, log evidence -640.4765 both. (5) TCPD F1 of 'no change' on the 7 held-out series from my own implementation of van den Burg & Williams (2020) F1 with margin 5 against the fetched annotations.json: 0.450/0.947/0.947/0.571/0.636/0.644/0.276, mean 0.639, exactly eval/tcpd-heldout.out.txt. Scored 4: the core matches the reference implementation exactly on every check; the many add-on tests (GARCH, synthetic control, hinge, known-date) were not independently recomputed.
evidence.completeness: Ran: `node cli.mjs --example` (agreed-changes line, segments, 95% range 1897-1899, BOCPD 79%), `--model poisson` on coal (1892, 1948 with ranges), `--ar1` on Lake Huron (no change; mean model alone gives 10), stdin input, the 3-row error ('Need at least 4 numbers; got 3', exit 2), watch.mjs on a growing Nile file (baseline then 'held, not alerted' for a change dated inside the quiet history, as documented), and `platform/agents/tools.mjs call changepoint-detector analyze` (values override the DEFAULTS csv; change at index 7, n 14). No TODO/FIXME in the 40 non-test modules. Page exposes every advertised option. The README's own 'Not verified' item (R changepoint) is still not done and is said so. Browser page not clicked through in this session.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/changepoint-detector: 1026 tests, 1026 pass, 0 fail, 315 s wall on 4 cores (was 343 tests / 524 s on 2026-11-09). Mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py against engine.test.mjs (baseline green, 39.5 s): BIC constant k ln n -> (k-0.5) ln n CAUGHT (14 of 86 tests fail; the 2026-11-09 thin-guard defect is closed); PELT prune bound F(s)+C <= F(t-1) dropped beta (over-pruning) CAUGHT; meanvar variance floor (sigma*1e-3)^2 -> (sigma*1e-1)^2 SURVIVED engine.test.mjs + meanvar-noise.test.mjs (the floor bites only on near-constant segments, which no test exercises at that scale). Tests include brute-force equality, closed-form evidence equality and ruptures/Poisson fixtures.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (pelt, peltMeanLoop, makeCost, robustSd, penaltyValue, bocpd, changeIntervals, analyze start), cli.mjs (301 lines). The PELT loop is careful and commented (deferred pruning with a perf note and a history doc for each optimisation). But engine.mjs has grown from 2243 to 3004 lines and still holds the core, BOCPD, five adjustment pipelines, GARCH search, burst/spike/excursion finders and report summaries; analyze() is ~360 lines; 225 test files and ~730 eval files sit flat in the venture root/eval with no runner config. A senior reviewer would ask for the module split before more features land.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: Nile/Cobb (reproduced), ruptures 100/100 (reproduced live), Poisson 90/90 fixture exists, 'BIC splits AR(1) rho 0.8 noise 40/40, 4/40 with --ar1' (fresh 200 series: 200/200 and 19/200 = 9.5%, consistent), range95 ~95% coverage, median width 4 at shift 2 (fresh 300 series: 97.3%, width 4), CLI/llms.txt TCPD held-out F1 0.711 / 0.296 / 0.639 and 31-series 0.706 / 0.702 / 0.714 / 0.663 / 0.477 (eval/tcpd-heldout.out.txt, eval/tcpd.out.txt; zero row recomputed). Disclaimer present on page (index.html:71) and README. Misses: the page FAQ (index.html:252 and the FAQPage JSON-LD at :12) says BIC 'rarely invents changes in long series', which the venture's own numbers contradict for real series (default level model 150 cuts on bitcoin, 167 on measles, held-out F1 0.296 vs 0.639 for no change; 200/200 false changes on AR(1)); README:82 says '581 tests on 2026-11-12' (now 1026); README:458 privacy lists 4 usage events, the page (index.html:266) lists 13. llms.txt example.invalid hosts are rewritten at deploy (source-only, not filed).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: an analyst with a CSV asks 'did this shift, when, how sure'. One command or one paste gives the agreed changes, segments, a 95% date range and a probability; sticky noise, seasons, trends, counts, clustered volatility and a named date each have an option, and watch.mjs turns it into a daily alert. Gaps: the option surface is very large and the README is an 8,396-line research log, so choosing settings relies on the page's agreed-changes default; the plain default level model is worse than 'no change' on real benchmark series, which the tool handles by leading with the agreed panel and an over-cut warning rather than changing the default.
evidence.domain: Compared with Killick et al. 2012, Adams & MacKay 2007, R changepoint penalty conventions ((params+1) ln n: 2 ln n mean, 3 ln n meanvar, matching) and ruptures. Exact on all recomputes. Departures a statistician would note are documented: noise sd fixed globally from MAD of differences, min segment 10 for meanvar, BOCPD probability read with a 5-point lag. Benchmarking against TCPD with the published F1/cover and a held-out set, pre-registration and negative results are above typical practice. On coal the Poisson BOCPD puts only 8% within 3 points of the 1892 change PELT finds, so the two methods can disagree on a textbook break; the agreed-changes logic is what reconciles them.

defects.what: Page FAQ says BIC 'rarely invents changes in long series'. The venture's own held-out benchmark shows the default level model at BIC cutting bitcoin 150 times and measles 167 times (F1 0.296 against 0.639 for reporting no change), and AR(1) noise gives a false change in 200 of 200 fresh series. True only for independent noise; the sentence should say so and point to the agreed changes / autocorrelation option. Also in the FAQPage JSON-LD at index.html:12.

verdict: Re-audited independently after substantial change (engine 2243 -> 3004 lines, tests 343 -> 1026). The statistical core is exact: my own optimal-partitioning DP and live ruptures 1.1.10 agree with the engine on Nile (mean and meanvar), coal-mining Poisson, Lake Huron and 120/120 fresh random series; my own Adams-MacKay recursion matches its BOCPD to 1e-11; the committed ruptures fixture regenerates 100/100; and the TCPD 'no change' baseline recomputes exactly (0.639). Fresh simulations reproduce the AR(1) false-alarm and range-coverage claims. All 1026 tests pass in 315 s; the BIC-constant guard flagged on 2026-11-09 is now caught by 14 tests (closed), and the 9-minute suite defect is much reduced; the meanvar variance floor mutation survives. Persisting: the monolithic engine (grown), the stale README test count, the research-log README. New: a page FAQ overclaim that BIC rarely invents changes in long series, contradicted by the venture's own benchmark. Meets the bar (correctness 4, claims 3, verification 3, median 3) and is finished; craft is the weak dimension.
